subject: Next steps: NimbleCare evaluation orchestration, exec readout & decision path
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (POC scope suggestions)

Hi Oliver — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before paperwork: 

1) Goal of the evaluation
- Validate Redwood’s ability to reduce median inference latency to under 120ms p50 on your peak query mix and to keep per-inference cost below $0.004 with 95% of traffic (target for the production plan).

2) Proposed success criteria (POC):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms on 8k rolling window with your dataset
- Accuracy: parity/within 2% of your current model baseline for the three primary intents (triage, summary, note-gen)
- Stability: <1% error rate over 48h of synthetic load + live shadowing
- Cost: measurable token cost reduction compared to current endpoint (we’ll run a cost-snapshot)

3) Evaluation plan and timeline
- Week 0 (next week): Access provisioning & sample dataset ingest (we provide S3 connector and ingestion checklist)
- Week 1: Baseline run + latency profiling (dry run)
- Week 2: Quantization / batching experiments + KV/prefix cache tuning
- Week 3: Live shadowing for acceptance (24–48h)
- Week 4: Readout and decision (exec review)

4) Owners
- Redwood (Irene): overall POC orchestration, infra setup, and readout presentation
- Redwood (Jordan): integration, telemetry dashboards, and cost analysis
- NimbleCare (Oliver): dataset access, acceptance checklist, procurement lead for contracting

5) Immediate asks from NimbleCare
- Grant S3 read-only access to sample bucket (IAM user or temporary STS)
- Confirm preferred exec readout window (we suggested Tue/Wed mornings PT week of Nov 23)

Attachments: POC success metrics worksheet + MOP draft attached for your review.

[Attachment: POC-success-metrics.docx (DOCX, 42KB)]
[Attachment: nimblecare-mop-v1.xlsx (Excel, 56KB)]

If this looks good I’ll loop in procurement/legal and kick off access steps on Monday.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (POC scope suggestions)

Thanks — got the redlines and the checklist. Quick decisions and next actions so we keep to the timeline: 

1) Data handling & deletion confirmations
- Redwood accepts the two-step deletion confirmation flow for the POC: (a) automated deletion after 30 days post-POC plus (b) manual confirmation email from our infra owner when deletion is completed. We will provide audit logs retention for 30 days as requested.

2) Indemnity/liability for POC stage
- We can accept a limited liability cap for the POC (mutually limited, not to exceed $25k) and a short phrase acknowledging trial-stage indemnity constraints. We’ll deliver a one-page addendum for signatures.

3) PO and procurement
- If procurement issues a non-binding PO for trial infra we’ll treat that as confirmation to reserve dedicated capacity for your shadow traffic window. Procurement — please confirm PO number when available.

4) Exec readout and decision process (Wed, 25 Nov, 10:00 PT)
- Outcome options: a) Go to pilot/contracting (requires exec sign-off + PO), b) Extend trial for one additional week with focused fixes, c) No-go.
- Exec readout deck: 15–20 minutes summary (Jordan: performance + cost), 10 minutes product/ops Q&A (Irene & Karthik). We’ll provide the readout deck by EOD Tue, Nov 24.

5) Action owners + timeline
- Monday (11/23): S3 creds + PO (if procurement ready)
- Tue (11/24): Baseline report + readout deck delivered to all stakeholders
- Wed (11/25): Exec readout 10:00–10:45 PT; immediate decision and next contract step discussion

Attachments: readout timeline + readout slide template.
